notes: Honda CR-V without the hybrid system, 2017 to 2021, from Honda U.S. service information. Many fuses and parts depend on trim, engine (1.5 L or 2.4 L), keyless access or auto idle stop, so check the legend's footnote for the vehicle in hand; the Hybrid has its own legend, not used here.

gaps: The PDF has no title page, Honda publication number or copyright notice; its Honda origin rests on the content, the article titles and the figure credit (Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.).
The archive item title says 2017 to 2023, but the fuse legend's year footnotes only name 2017-19, 2018-21 and 2020-21, so years are set to 2017-2021.
Battery CCA is not printed, so no CCA claim; the amps in part specs are circuit fuse ratings, not motor ratings. No alternator, starter or fan motor ratings were claimed.
Fuse footnotes make many positions trim-, engine- or keyless-access-specific; specs give ranges and examples, not every footnote.
The relay chart does not say which box each relay sits in.
method: Honda CR-V 2017 to 2023 RW RT Service Manual, Internet Archive item honda-cr-v-2017-to-2023-rw-rt-service-manual (community upload; PDF about 430 MB, 14,934 pages), downloaded and read with pdftotext; fuse and relay pages also rendered as images.
Every page carries a GetTheManuals.org watermark. The PDF is a compiled export of Honda U.S. service information: articles are titled with the model and (Hybrid) or (Except Hybrid).
Battery size: PDF p. 7452. Fuse legends: PDF pp. 7461-7475, inside the article Electrical System - Testing & Troubleshooting - CR-V (Except Hybrid), which starts at p. 7446.
Relay chart: PDF p. 1481, in the article Exterior Lighting - Testing & Troubleshooting - CR-V (Except Hybrid), which starts at p. 1462.
A second fuse legend at PDF pp. 7559-7566 belongs to the Hybrid (A1-7 is 150 A there) and was not used.
The researcher reported that Honda's owner's manual at techinfo.honda.com failed its TLS certificate check; it was not used and not re-tested.

comps.spec: 12 V battery, size 55B24, L2, as listed in the manual's parasitic draw check (PDF p. 7452)
Radiator fan motor: 30 A fuse A1-3 in the under-hood box, via the radiator fan relay (PDF p. 7462)
A/C condenser fan motor: 30 A fuse A2-6 in the under-hood box, via the A/C condenser fan relay (PDF p. 7463)
Fuel pump: 15 A fuse D8 in the under-dash box, via PGM-FI main relay 2; the same fuse also covers the body control module, the immobilizer-keyless control unit and other loads (PDF pp. 7470-7471)

Starter: 30 A fuse A3-5 in the under-hood box, through the starter cut relay circuits; on 2.4 L engines a 7.5 A fuse C28 for the starter solenoid diode sits in fuse/relay holder B (PDF pp. 7463, 7467)
Blower motor: 40 A fuse A3-1 in the under-hood box (PDF p. 7463)
Windshield wiper control unit/motor: 30 A fuse A2-5 in the under-hood box (PDF p. 7463)
Rear window wiper motor: 5 A fuse D4 in the under-dash box with keyless access, 5 A fuse D17 without it (PDF pp. 7469, 7472)
EPS motor/control unit: 70 A fuse A2-1 in the under-hood box (PDF p. 7462)

Power relays in the relay test chart. Four-terminal type (20 listed): A/C compressor clutch, A/C condenser fan, front blower motor, horn, injector, PGM-FI main 2, power window, radiator fan, rear window defogger and others. Five-terminal type: ACC cut, fan control, IG2 cut (PDF p. 1481)

Under-hood box A1-1 to A24: 43 positions, 7.5 to 125 A (A1-2 40 A brake booster; A1-7 125 A, protects most A3, A4, A18-A24 fuses). Under-dash box D1 to D39: 5 to 20 A. Auxiliary E1 to E8: 20 A (E6, E7 unused); F1 to F7 (auto idle stop): 5 to 15 A. Holders B25-B27, C28-C30, G31-G36

Audio unit (without navigation), audio-navigation unit (with) and center display unit (display audio type): 15 A fuse A19 in the under-hood box without auto idle stop, 30 A fuse B27 with it. Stereo amplifier: 30 A A1-1 without it, 20 A E5 with it (PDF pp. 7461-7462, 7465-7467, 7474)
